transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Avery Li (Redwood CSM), Ethan Rivers (CTO, Aquilo), Maya Lopez (Head of ML), Samir Khan (DevOps), Priya Desai (Product)

Summary (auto):
Customer evaluating migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated for production chat/agents. Primary concerns: eval parity vs current models, latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/networking, SSO/KMS requirements, and pilot scope. Action items and benchmark plan agreed.

Topics:
- Current OpenAI footprint and costs
- Model/eval parity and compatibility (vLLM/TGI considerations)
- Dedicated capacity sizing and autoscaling
- Network/security: VPC, SAML, KMS, audit logs
- Next steps: benchmarks, pricing, pilot kickoff

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side, with Jordan our SE and Avery from CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Ethan Rivers: Good, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in, we've been trying to get this lined up.
[00:11] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda — we wanted to understand your current stack, constraints, and what success looks like moving off OpenAI to either Redwood Hosted or Dedicated, maybe Private down the line. Jordan will dig into technical fit.
[00:22] Maya Lopez: Sounds good. I'll give a quick overview of where we're at. We run customer support and in-product agents. Currently all generation goes through OpenAI gpt-4 for both chat and summarization. Our monthly spend is significant and we're seeing bursts that break our rate limits.
[00:37] Priya Desai: And from product side we need deterministic latency under 400ms p95 for interactive features, and cost per 1k tokens is a big lever for scaling.
[00:47] Jordan Patel: Understood. When you say p95 400ms, is that for short context, like 256 tokens, or longer multi-turn?
[00:54] Maya Lopez: Mostly short interactions, 128-256 tokens. We do some longer summarization jobs in batch.
[01:01] Jordan Patel: Okay. Could you share current qps and token volume?
[01:05] Samir Khan: Right now ~12 qps average, peaks to 60 qps during campaign windows. Tokens vary but about 300M tokens monthly across models.
[01:14] Jordan Patel: That's helpful. For those volumes, Dedicated reserved capacity usually makes sense — predictable throughput and cost. We can size GPU pools with auto-scale and burst for peaks.
[01:24] Ethan Rivers: How compatible is Redwood with our existing prompts and tooling? We use some community stacks with vLLM for inference internally for tests, and TGI for a few hosted models. Concern is eval parity: our prompts tuned on OpenAI gpt-4 must behave similarly on any new infra.
[01:41] Jordan Patel: Totally. Two parts: model compatibility and operational compatibility. On model side, we onboarding curated open models and we also support model variants that aim for eval parity. We often run the customer's eval set — if you share the prompt corpus we can run a parity report. On infra, Redwood supports similar API shapes and we provide SDKs. Some customers run vLLM/TGI locally for dev, and we map those to Redwood endpoints; occasionally tokens/stop sequences need small tweaks — common mis-encoding or temperature differences.
[02:06] Maya Lopez: Any examples of parity numbers? We've seen some vendors claim 95% but it's fuzzy.
[02:11] Jordan Patel: In our experience parity can range 90-99% depending on prompt types and model selection. For QA and retrieval-augmented tasks we usually get high match. We'll run your exact suite and produce a delta table. Note: sometimes hallucination patterns change and we add a small calibration layer.
[02:26] Priya Desai: What about latency — you mentioned GPU pools. Are there SLOs we can expect?
[02:30] Jordan Patel: For Dedicated we set targets (e.g., 100-200ms token throughput for short contexts depending on model and GPU). We'll validate with your workload; the benchmark run will give realistic p95 numbers. Also we have prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated context cost and latency.
[02:44] Ethan Rivers: How does batching impact latency? We're very latency sensitive.
[02:48] Jordan Patel: There's a tradeoff: batching increases throughput and lowers cost but can add tail latency. Dedicated allows you to configure batching policies and smart routing — for interactive endpoints we recommended minimal batching and KV caching. For bulk jobs, aggressive batching is fine.
[02:59] Samir Khan: Network and security question — we have strict VPC peering and internal-only egress. We need SAML SSO for console, RBAC, and KMS integration for keys. Also audit logs retention for 12 months.
[03:13] Avery Li: On the security side, Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) supports customer-managed networking, and Dedicated can be deployed into a VPC with private connectivity. We support SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations; audit logs and SOC2 docs are available. We'll share the security pack after the call (link: https://redwood.example/security-pack.pdf).
[03:31] Ethan Rivers: Good. Also curious about model ops — if we pin a model version and there's a regression, what's rollback look like?
[03:38] Maya Chen: We expose rollouts and can do canary deploys or automatic fallback to a previous pinned model. The console gives per-route metrics and regressions alerts if quality drops on a supplied eval set.
[03:48] Maya Lopez: For our team, the biggest risk is behavioral drift. If you can prove parity on our eval set that's critical.
[03:54] Jordan Patel: Agreed. We'll run the eval parity and include a quality monitor in the pilot. If you share the eval set, we'll return a CSV with exact diffs and examples.
[04:03] Priya Desai: How about cost modeling — can we get an estimate of unit cost vs OpenAI?
[04:08] Maya Chen: Yes. We'll send a pricing sheet and a modeled comparison given your volumes. Dedicated often lowers per-token costs substantially at your scale, but depends on model choice and utilization.
[04:18] Ethan Rivers: Are there blockers moving from the OpenAI API shape? We have tooling built around their request/response.
[04:24] Jordan Patel: We support similar REST shapes and SDKs; we also have adapters for common frameworks. The biggest differences are model names, sometimes stop token handling and streaming boundaries — minor code changes in most cases. We can provide a migration guide and example diff.
[04:38] Samir Khan: For the pilot we need to run a smoke test in our staging VPC and measure p95 and cost over a week. We also want to run some stress tests to verify autoscaling.
[04:49] Jordan Patel: That aligns with our standard pilot: 1) sandbox integration (staging), 2) run benchmarks with your eval prompts, 3) validate autoscale and networking, 4) go to production canary. Typical pilot length is 2-4 weeks.
[04:59] Ethan Rivers: Do you support bring-your-own-model (BYOM) with custom weights? Some of our research runs custom fine-tunes.
[05:06] Jordan Patel: We support private model hosting and bring-your-own-model in Dedicated/Private, including custom weights and quantization profiles. We also help with kernel selection and quantization recommendations to optimize latency.
[05:17] Priya Desai: Anything about regulatory compliance — data residency, encryption at rest?
[05:22] Avery Li: Dedicated can be provisioned in specific regions; Private on-prem addresses residency requirements. We support encryption at-rest and in-transit and KMS/HSM integrations for key management.
[05:33] Maya Lopez: One more — we've experimented with running vLLM in-house for some workloads. It was faster for small contexts but the ops burden is high. How does Redwood compare?
[05:43] Jordan Patel: vLLM/TGI are great for experimentation; Redwood's runtime optimizes kernels, continuous batching, and caching with much less ops overhead. You get the lower tail latency plus managed reliability. For customers that want we can run hybrid where devs use vLLM locally and production uses Redwood Dedicated.
[05:58] Ethan Rivers: Ok that helps. Let's talk about concrete next steps.
[06:02] Maya Chen: Proposed: Samir shares sample prompts and a week of usage logs; Jordan runs benchmark and returns p95/cost numbers; Maya to send pricing; Avery to schedule pilot kickoff.
[06:12] Priya Desai: That works. Prefer kickoff next Tue if possible.
[06:15] Avery Li: I'll send a calendar invite for 2026-03-10.
[06:19] Jordan Patel: Quick note on bench run — please include the top 50 prompts by volume and any context windows so we can emulate caching and prefix hits.
[06:28] Samir Khan: Will do, sending by end of day tomorrow.
[06:32] Ethan Rivers: On competitors — we've looked at Anthropic for safety claims and Azure OpenAI for marketplace convenience. OpenAI is entrenched but costs are getting painful.
[06:43] Maya Chen: Totally. We often see customers start with Hosted and then Dedicated when they hit predictable scale. For regulated workloads Private is an option.
[06:51] Priya Desai: Any rough numbers on cost reduction?
[06:54] Maya Chen: It varies, but at your volumes customers typically see 25-60% cost savings on per-token when moving to Dedicated with right model and utilization. We'll run exact projections.
[07:05] Jordan Patel: Last technical nit — we sometimes see transcripts where libs refer to KV cache as K V cash or stop tokens being mis-handled; just flagging that prompts with weird control chars can change behavior, worth sanitizing.
[07:18] Maya Lopez: Noted. We'll sanitize.
[07:21] Ethan Rivers: Great recap. If we get parity within 5% and network/SSO checks out, we can move to pilot.
[07:29] Maya Chen: Excellent. We'll follow up with the benchmark template, pricing, and security pack. Anything else?
[07:34] Priya Desai: No, that's it from us.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
